checks.name: book layer 1
checks.observed:
01 / SETUP
Keys made for one compiled relation

Groth16 derives proving and verifying keys from secret randomness for one compiled circuit. Each distinct compiled relation needs its own setup; the count follows circuits, not predicates or catalogue entries. Whoever keeps that randomness can forge proofs, so soundness assumes it is destroyed.

What this layer produces

Proving key and verifying key

checks.name: book layer 2
checks.observed:
02 / LANGUAGE
Financial rules written as a program

Moriarty programs state what an action may do: payment arithmetic, fees kept separate from repayment, caps an owner signs, and duties that continue. The compiler turns that source into constraints; a rule left unconstrained is a rule no proof enforces.

checks.observed:
03 / WITNESS
Every step, recorded by the prover

The prover runs the program over its inputs and records every intermediate value. Zero-knowledge keeps this assignment hidden, but only the assignment: amounts that appear in Cardano outputs or in the statement stay public. Witness generation must not leak values through its own behavior.

checks.name: book layer 4
checks.observed:
04 / ARITHMETIZATION
Every rule becomes an equation

The compiled program becomes rank-1 constraints over a prime field, which Groth16 encodes as a quadratic arithmetic program. A valid witness satisfies every constraint. The public inputs carry a statement digest; an in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget ties them to the statement bytes.

checks.name: book layer 5
checks.observed:
05 / PROOF SYSTEM
A short certificate of correct computation

Groth16 turns the witness into a constant-size proof checked by one pairing equation. Under an honest setup, knowledge soundness means a verifying proof shows the prover knew a satisfying witness; zero-knowledge means the proof reveals nothing beyond its statement. It never shows the statement's values describe the real ledger.

checks.name: book layer 6
checks.observed:
06 / CRYPTOGRAPHIC BEDROCK
Hard problems underneath

A pairing-friendly elliptic curve supplies Groth16's groups and scalar field; Groth16's soundness argument holds in the generic bilinear group model. BLAKE2b collision resistance binds statement bytes to digests. Signatures authenticate owner intents and claimant releases. These primitives support the proof core and fix what it can express.

checks.name: book layer 7
checks.observed:
07 / VERIFICATION
Proof meets ledger

A claim policy checks each Groth16 proof and mints a proof-claim output. One settlement transaction consumes every Strand the Web requires; the validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and spent state, requires claimant signatures and enforces signed caps. Outside facts need a named issuer, authentication path and freshness limit.

checks.name: hypothetical circuit count8
checks.observed:
1 shared phase 1 + 8 phase 2

8 circuits need one shared phase 1 and 8 circuit-specific phase 2 stages. That counts stages; it does not mean 8 + 1 complete ceremonies.

This holds only if every circuit uses the same curve, fits the phase-1 capacity and accepts its format, and only if each phase has a verified transcript with at least one honest participant.
